title: The village that said 'enough'
instructions: Read the article about a small village and the cruise ships that visit it. Some sentences have been removed from the text. Choose the most suitable sentence (A–K) for each gap (1–8). There are two extra sentences that you do not need to use. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Olvasd el a cikket egy kis faluról és az oda érkező tengerjáró hajókról. Néhány mondatot kivettünk a szövegből: válaszd ki minden hiányhoz (1–8) az odaillő mondatot (A–K). Két mondat felesleges. A 0. a példa.

passage.title: The village that said 'enough'
passage.subtitle: How a tiny Norwegian community took on the cruise industry – and what happened next

blocks.text: On a still morning in early spring, Vestvik looks like a picture from a tourist brochure: a few dozen wooden houses painted red and white, a tiny harbour, and steep mountains rising straight out of the dark water of the fjord. [[0]] Until three years ago, however, on a summer's day this village of 380 people could receive as many as 6,000 visitors, most of them arriving on cruise ships so large that they blocked the view of the mountains from almost every kitchen window.

For a long time, nobody complained. The ships brought money to a place that had been slowly emptying since its fish processing plant closed in the 1990s. [[1]] But as the number of ships grew from one season to the next, the benefits became harder to see. 'Most passengers stayed for four hours, walked up to the waterfall, took a photo and went back on board for lunch,' says Ole Brekke, who runs the village's only café. 'They didn't eat here, they didn't sleep here. What they left behind was traffic and rubbish.'

There were less visible costs, too. The ships kept their engines running while they were in port, and on windless days a brownish haze hung over the fjord. [[2]] Residents began to joke that they would soon need a ticket to walk to their own post office. For many, the final straw came in the summer of 2022, when an ambulance took forty minutes to reach an elderly man who had collapsed in his garden, because the only road was blocked by tour buses.

That autumn, Kari Lunde, a former primary school teacher who had been elected mayor only a year earlier, called a public meeting. She expected perhaps fifty people. [[3]] After three hours of heated discussion, the village agreed on a plan that would have seemed unthinkable a decade earlier: from 2024, only one cruise ship would be allowed to dock per day, with no more than 1,000 passengers on board, and it would have to plug into electricity from the shore instead of running its engines.

The cruise companies reacted angrily. Two of them announced that they would drop Vestvik from their routes altogether, and a regional newspaper predicted that the village would 'die a second death'. [[4]] In the first summer under the new rules, the number of visitors fell by almost seventy per cent, and Brekke's café took less money than in any year since he had opened it.

Then something unexpected happened. Visitors who arrived by other means – on foot, by bicycle or on the local ferry – began to stay longer. [[5]] Guesthouses that used to be empty in July, because nobody wanted to spend the night next to a floating hotel, were suddenly fully booked. By the second summer, Brekke's takings were higher than they had ever been. 'One hiker who stays three nights spends more here than fifty cruise passengers,' he says.

Dr Paolo Ferri, a tourism researcher who has studied similar cases in Italy and Croatia, believes that Vestvik's experience holds a lesson for many other destinations. 'For years, the industry measured success simply by counting heads,' he says. [[6]] He also points out that Vestvik had an unusual advantage. [[7]] Few other places have that luxury: in large cities, ports are often controlled by national authorities, and far more jobs depend on mass tourism.

Not everyone in Vestvik is happy with the new reality. Some older residents miss the bustle of the busy summers, and the souvenir shop on the harbour has closed. [[8]] Lunde, for her part, has no regrets. 'We did not ban tourists,' she says. 'We decided what kind of tourism we wanted. That is a right every community should have.'

options.text: Without the crowds, Vestvik had become exactly the kind of peaceful place they had been hoping to find.
On busy days, the café ran out of food long before lunchtime.
Meanwhile, the narrow lanes between the houses became so crowded that locals could hardly get through them.
It is easy to understand why travel magazines regularly describe it as one of the most beautiful spots in Europe.
Its owner, who had put all his savings into the business, says the village has chosen peace and quiet over jobs.
Instead, more than two hundred people turned up, and the meeting had to be moved from the town hall to the school gym.
'What really matters is how long visitors stay, how much of their money remains in the community and whether local people can still live a normal life.'
As a result, the guesthouses in the village were forced to close one after another.
A souvenir shop opened on the harbour, and for the first time in years teenagers could find summer jobs without leaving home.
Because the harbour belongs to the municipality, the decision about which ships could dock there was entirely in local hands.
Even some residents who had voted for the plan began to fear that the newspaper might be right.

example.explanation: D. Az előző mondat leírja, milyen gyönyörű a falu (mint egy turistaprospektus képe); a D ehhez kapcsolódik: érthető, hogy az utazási magazinok Európa egyik legszebb helyének tartják. Az utána következő „however” (azonban) erre a szép képre ad ellenpontot a tömegekkel.
example.evidence: Vestvik looks like a picture from a tourist brochure

items.explanation: I. Az előző mondat szerint a hajók pénzt hoztak a néptelenedő faluba; az I konkrét példát ad erre (megnyílt egy ajándékbolt, a tinédzserek nyári munkát kaptak). Az utána következő „But … the benefits became harder to see” ezekre az előnyökre utal vissza. Az ajándékbolt az utolsó bekezdésben is előkerül („the souvenir shop on the harbour”).
items.evidence: The ships brought money to a place that had been slowly emptying

wrongOptions.B: Csábító, mert a forgalomról szól, de ellentmond Brekke szavainak: az utasok nem ettek a faluban („They didn't eat here”), és visszamentek a hajóra ebédelni.

items.explanation: C. A bekezdés a kevésbé látható költségeket sorolja (szennyezett levegő), a „Meanwhile” (közben) egy újabb gondot vezet be: a zsúfolt utcákat. Erre utal a következő mondat tréfája, hogy hamarosan jegy kell majd a saját postájukhoz, és a buszok miatt elakadó mentő is.
items.evidence: Residents began to joke that they would soon need a ticket to walk to their own post office.

wrongOptions.B: A zsúfoltsághoz illene, de ellentmond a szövegnek: az utasok nem ettek a faluban („They didn't eat here”), így a kávézóban sem fogyhatott el miattuk az étel.

items.explanation: F. Lunde legfeljebb ötven emberre számított; az „Instead” (ehelyett) ezzel áll szemben: több mint kétszázan jöttek el, ezért át kellett költözniük az iskola tornatermébe. Ezután jön a háromórás heves vita.

wrongOptions.K: Itt még nincs megszavazott terv (csak a gyűlés után fogadják el), és az újságról sem esett még szó – a K a következő bekezdésbe, az újság jóslata után illik.

items.explanation: K. Az előző mondatban a regionális újság azt jósolja, hogy a falu „másodszor is meghal”; a K erre utal vissza („the newspaper might be right”): még a terv egyes támogatói is félni kezdtek. A következő mondat (70%-kal kevesebb látogató) igazolja a félelmüket.
items.evidence: a regional newspaper predicted that the village would 'die a second death'

wrongOptions.H: Csábító, mert negatív következményről szól, de ellentmond a szövegnek: a vendégházak később „fully booked”, tehát nem zártak be. Ráadásul az „As a result” itt nem kapcsolódna semmilyen okhoz.

items.explanation: A. Az előző mondat szerint a más módon (gyalog, biciklivel, komppal) érkezők tovább maradtak; az A megmagyarázza, miért: a tömeg nélkül a falu éppen olyan nyugodt hely lett, amilyet kerestek. A „they” ezekre a látogatókra utal, és a teltházas vendégházak is ezt folytatják.
items.evidence: Visitors who arrived by other means – on foot, by bicycle or on the local ferry – began to stay longer.

wrongOptions.H: A vendégházak itt épp, hogy megteltek („were suddenly fully booked”), tehát a bezárásukról szóló mondat ellentmondana a szövegnek.

items.explanation: G. Ferri azt mondja, hogy az iparág a sikert sokáig csak a fejek számolásával mérte; a G idézete ezt folytatja és ellenpontozza: ami valóban számít, az a tartózkodás hossza, a helyben maradó pénz és a helyiek normális élete.
items.evidence: 'For years, the industry measured success simply by counting heads,' he says.

wrongOptions.J: A J a következő hiányba illik: csak a „Vestvik had an unusual advantage” mondat után van értelme, mert az nevezi meg, mi ez az előny.

items.explanation: J. Az előző mondat bejelenti, hogy Vestviknek szokatlan előnye volt; a J megmondja, mi ez: a kikötő a községé, így a döntés teljesen helyi kézben volt. Az utána következő „that luxury” erre utal vissza, mert a nagyvárosokban a kikötőket gyakran országos hatóságok irányítják.
items.evidence: He also points out that Vestvik had an unusual advantage.

wrongOptions.G: A G idézete nem nevez meg semmilyen előnyt, és a „that luxury” sem utalhatna rá – ez a mondat az előző hiányba, a „counting heads” után illik.

items.explanation: E. Az előző mondat szerint bezárt a kikötői ajándékbolt; az „Its owner” (a tulajdonosa) erre a boltra utal: minden megtakarítását belefektette, és szerinte a falu a csendet választotta a munkahelyek helyett. Ez az elégedetlen hang áll szemben Lunde véleményével („for her part, has no regrets”).
items.evidence: the souvenir shop on the harbour has closed

wrongOptions.K: Témában illene az elégedetlenekhez, de múlt idejű és az újság jóslatára utal („the newspaper”), ami a 4. hiány környezetében szerepel; itt az „Its owner” köti a mondatot a bezárt bolthoz.
